Increased employment and income for artisanal and small-scale mining enterprises (ASMEs), and in particular increased economic opportunities for women participating in ASMEs throughout the Development Minerals value chain Output 1: - A firm was successfully contracted to develop a strategy for formalization and business development acceleration for the Development Minerals sector in Uganda. The process was concluded end-Feb, 2021.
Output 2: - Three firms have been awarded grants to pilot inclusive business eco-system project targeting youth in Uganda.
Output 3: N/A
Output 4: - Study on enhancing womens participation in the Development Minerals sector in Uganda has been finalised and printed for dissemination in different fora.
Output 5: Various knowledge sharing events were held to showcase opportunities for youth in the extractives sector including development minerals as well as to highlight the issue and solutions to gender-based violence in the context of women in mining. In total, over 500 youth were reached over online engagements platforms and over 300,000 Ugandans were reached over social media; tv broadcast and 100 YouTube views with messaging on financing mineral value chains for women and addressing GBV in the mining sector.

Output 1: Institutions in ACP countries have improved business enabling environment for gender-inclusive operationalization and formalization of ASMEs (Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining Enterprises) along the Development Minerals value chain. Progress/results attained under output one (1) -Formalization of ASMEs (Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining Enterprises) is ongoing. 125 sets of by-laws have been secured to aid the formalization of the target ASMEs. The formalization activity is targeting 125 ASMEs in Uganda and will be completed by February 2023. -14 (11M/3F) stakeholders were trained in geodata mapping and reserve estimation of development minerals in Uganda. Four (4) sites and materials were also assessed for geodata and reserve estimation, which has enriched Ugandas catalogue of development minerals especially in informing policy and investment decisions. The sites that were mapped are located in Rwampara district (Sand), Kasese district (Aggregates), Mubende (Dimension stone) and Alebtong district (Clay).
Output 2: ASMEs have enhanced entrepreneurial skills and access to finance, technology, markets and market information; and better regulations. Progress/results attained under output two (2) -198 ASMEs and Associations in 25 districts of Uganda have been equipped with knowledge and skills in enterprise development, business management and financial literacy. The training directly reached 487 miners in a trainer of trainer (TOT) approach that facilitated further training of 2,750 artisanal and small-scale miners. -Two (2) SMEs – Kajana Limited and Nkokonjeru Area Cooperative Limited (NACE) have been supported to adopt inclusive business models for product development and value addition. This support has been delivered through grants. The two SMEs received grants to improve value and supply chains through adoption of technologies for innovation and increased production. The projects are being implemented in Lira and Mityana districts. - One (1) company – Hamlet Uganda Limited- has been supported, through a grant, to pilot a digital solution to enhance access to markets and market information; and appropriate technologies in the Development Minerals sector. The company is developing an online platform that will bridge the market and information gap about construction materials; as well as onboard ASM sites onto the platform to facilitate easier trade in their products and services.
Output 3: Public institutions, communities, women’s organizations and civil society organizations (CSOs) have strengthened capacity to put in place social and environmental safeguards in mining and quarrying of Development Minerals. Progress/results attained under output three (3) -340 ASMEs have been trained on Mine and Quarry Management -340 ASMEs have been trained and have developed return-to-work plans on Occupational Health and Safety and Environmental Management; and gender inclusion -340 ASME operators have been trained and are implementing improved community engagement/conflict management and protection of human rights/labor/gender/child rights in their respective sites of operation.
Output 4: Women-owned ASMEs are supported to operate in the Development Minerals value-chains. Progress made/results attained under output four (4) -66 women owned/led ASMEs have been trained in selected value chains, value addition and marketing. The training activities have been implemented in 4 regions and 25 districts of Uganda namely; 1) Eastern Region; Jinja, Tororo, Bukedea, Soroti, Moroto and Amudat . 2) Central Region; Wakiso, Kampala, Masaka, Mubende, Mukono and Luwero. 3) Northern Region; Lira, Arua, Kitgum, Gulu, Alebtong and Dokolo 4) Western Region Kasese, Fortpotal, Ibanda, Mbarara, Bushenyi, Rubirizi and Rwampara.
Output 5: Inter-ACP knowledge generation and dissemination are enhanced to inform policies, strategies and programmes for supporting ASMEs Results attained under output five (5) -46 local government officials demonstrated increased knowledge and positive attitude towards ASMEs through supporting the training programmes in their respective districts. The officials include the district commercial officers and district natural resources officers who comprised part of the training teams. This approach facilitated improved knowledge about ASMEs operating the target communities and their needs in terms of technical services, oversight and support.
